messages:
Ava: Quick Q for offer letter copy. Contractor starts 11/10 and may accrue a small sick balance before offboarding. Can we promise conversion to a floating holiday or cash-out? Need exact wording.

Olivia (People Ops): Short: do not promise conversion. Sick accruals are contract-dependent. We can approve a one-time exception in rare cases but it requires manager + People Ops (+ Legal for contracts) approval.

Ravi (Eng): Is the process different for contractors vs employees?

Olivia (People Ops): Yes. W-2s follow state law (often no payout). Contractors depend on SOW; we can amend a contract but Legal must review.

Tara (Hiring): For offers, would this wording work: "Unused sick may be considered for a one-time exception by People Ops and Finance; not guaranteed."

Olivia (People Ops): That looks good. Add: "for contractors, subject to contract amendment and Legal review."

Ava: Got it. Second item: product launch 12/18. Someone asked for 12/15-12/17 off. Any chance for a blackout exception?

Ravi (Eng): Standard rule: deny PTO within two weeks of launch unless coverage is documented. If the IC can be on-call and we have explicit coverage, manager can request an exception.

Olivia (People Ops): Process: manager submits an exception ticket with a short coverage plan (who covers, how rollbacks/merge/fix handled, confirmation IC can be reachable). People Ops reviews for fairness. If approved, we often grant a compensatory floating day after launch.

Lina (Payroll): Payroll note: compensatory day is applied manually. People Ops tells Payroll the employee ID and date, and we add the day within two pay cycles. Cutoff for Nov payroll is 11/28 for any payouts.

Ava: Thanks. I'll keep the offer conservative and include the exception path.

people-ops-bot: Exception ticket created #HR-2026-378. Please attach manager approval and coverage plan. Triage in 2 business days.

Olivia (People Ops): Thanks team. Ava 9— ping me when the manager sign-off is in the ticket and I'll route Legal if we need a contract amendment. :white_check_mark:
